## Purpose and scope

This protocol measures the concentration of double-stranded DNA in many samples at once (DNA extracts, PCR products, libraries in 96-well format) with Quant-iT PicoGreen and the FLUOstar Omega plate reader. For single samples use EnGeL-MOLB-QUBIT; for purity use EnGeL-MOLB-NANODROP.

## Principle

PicoGreen fluoresces strongly only when bound to double-stranded DNA. The fluorescence of each well is compared with a standard curve made from a dilution series of lambda DNA, so the result is specific to dsDNA. The lab uses half the volumes of the manufacturer's assay (100 µL per well) with the same high-range standards.

| Item | Details |
|:--|:--|

| Sample volume | 2 µL per well |

## Reagent preparation

- **1X TE:** dilute 20X TE 1:20 in nuclease-free water (e.g. 2.5 mL 20X TE + 47.5 mL water for 50 mL).
- **Lambda working stock (2 ng/µL = 2 µg/mL):** dilute the 100 µg/mL lambda DNA 50-fold in 1X TE, e.g. 10 µL Lambda DNA + 490 µL 1X TE for 500 µL (the earlier lab version, 9 µL + 441 µL, gives 450 µL at the same concentration).
- **PicoGreen working reagent:** dilute 1:200 in 1X TE, fresh on the day, in the dark. Per 96-well plate, prepare 5 mL: 25 µL PicoGreen + 4 975 µL 1X TE (50 µL per well).

**Standard curve (in duplicate)**

<!-- bench -->
**PicoGreen standards.**

| Standard | Lambda working stock (µL) | 1X TE (µL) | Working reagent (µL) | Concentration (ng/mL) |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| S1 | 50 | 0 | 50 | 1000 |
| S2 | 5 | 45 | 50 | 100 |
| S3 | 0.5 | 49.5 | 50 | 10 |
| Blank | 0 | 50 | 50 | 0 |

## Procedure

### Before starting

- Use filter tips at all steps; plastic tubes only.
- Keep the PicoGreen reagent and working reagent protected from light.

### Plate and reading

(@) Pipette each standard into the black plate in duplicate (table in Reagent preparation).
(@) Samples: 2 µL sample + 48 µL 1X TE per well + 50 µL working reagent.
(@) Mix by pipetting or a short plate shake.
(@) Incubate for 2 min at room temperature, protected from light.
(@) Plate reader: *Manage Protocol* → “PicoGREEN_LC_100”; *Start measurement* → *Gain Adjustment*; then *Start measurement*. The reader protocol is a fluorescence-intensity endpoint read (Greiner 96 F-bottom plate; excitation filter 485-12, emission filter 520; top optic; 30 flashes per well; settling time 0.5 s). The gain is set at 80–90% of the highest standard (1 000 ng/mL), and the blank is subtracted in the evaluation.
(@) In the reader software, fit a linear regression of the standards (S1–S3 and blank) (*Calculation* → *Standard curve calculations* → *Linear regression fit*); then, in *Microplate View*, select *Linear Regression Fit* under *Recalculate concentration*.

### After finishing

{{< include ../../includes/_before-you-leave.qmd >}}

## Calculations

**Sample concentration**

$$c_\mathrm{sample} = \frac{c_\mathrm{well} \times 50}{1000}$$

- $c_\mathrm{sample}$: concentration of the sample (ng/µL)
- $c_\mathrm{well}$: concentration read from the standard curve (ng/mL)
- 50: dilution of the sample in the well (2 µL in 100 µL; dimensionless)
- 1000: conversion from ng/mL to ng/µL

**Worked example** (illustrative value): a well reads 400 ng/mL → 400 × 50 / 1000 = 20 ng/µL.

## Quality control

| Control | Purpose | Acceptance criterion |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Standard curve (S1–S3 + blank, in duplicate) | Calibration | R² ≥ 0.99; if not, prepare the standards again and repeat the curve before reading the samples |
| Samples within the curve | Valid reading | Above S1 (1 000 ng/mL in the well): dilute in 1X TE and measure again. Below the lowest standard: report as below the curve |
| DNA concentration of extracts | Enough DNA for PCR | General rule: ≥ 10 ng/µL success; < 5 ng/µL fail; depends on the starting quantity and parent material; between 5 and 10 ng/µL the PCR result decides |

## Data and metadata

- **Outputs:** dsDNA concentration (ng/µL) per well; plate-reader export with the standard curve.
- **Where:** the *Sample_Tracking* sheet of the Metabarcoding Lab Pipeline workbook (DNA_ngul) or the project's records, and the lab book; instrument use in the QC user log.

::: {.callout-note title="Minimum to record"}
- Plate ID and plate map (EnGeL sample labels); date; operator
- PicoGreen kit lot; reader protocol used
- Standard curve R²; concentrations (ng/µL), marked as PicoGreen values

## Safety and waste

{{< include ../../includes/_safety-general.qmd >}}

- PicoGreen is dissolved in DMSO, which passes through skin, and binds DNA: wear gloves; keep away from light [TO CONFIRM: hazards from the SDS].

**Waste**

{{< include ../../includes/_waste-streams.qmd >}}

For this protocol: plates, tubes and tips go to biological solid waste (black bin) [TO CONFIRM].

## Troubleshooting

| Problem | Likely cause | Solution |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Standard curve R² < 0.99 | Pipetting error in the standards, or old lambda working stock | Prepare the standards again and repeat the curve. |
| Low signal overall | Reagent exposed to light, or glass tubes used | Prepare the working reagent fresh, in the dark, in plastic tubes. |
| Samples above S1 | Concentration beyond the curve | Dilute the samples in 1X TE and measure again; correct for the dilution. |

## Remarks

The manual uses a 200 µL assay (100 µL sample + 100 µL working reagent); the lab uses half volumes (100 µL), with the same high-range standards (1 µg/mL, 100 ng/mL, 10 ng/mL, blank). For very dilute samples the manual gives a low-range curve (25 ng/mL to 250 pg/mL).
